newsitem.title: USA: U.S. OPTIONS FOCUS/No surprises in index options.
newsitem.headline: U.S. OPTIONS FOCUS/No surprises in index options.

text.p: Index options volume was on the high side but the action was unspectacular, traders said Thursday.
By 1500 CDT (2000 GMT), a total of 231,896 index options traded on the Chicago Board Options exchange. The action was fairly even, with call volume coming in at 119,195 and put volume at 112,701.
"It looks like normal activity right around the strike," said Michael Schwartz, managing director at Oppenheimer & Co, citing the S&P 100 index 660, 665 and 670 options.
The OEX ended down a fraction at 661.58 after trading between 659.35 and 666.58.

Although OEX call volume outpaced put volume, the busiest OEX option was the October 660 put, which traded about 12,360 contracts. The next most active was the October 670 call, with 11,875 contracts traded.
Traders said the activity in those two options was split evenly between buyers and sellers, with no particular strategy involved.
Schwartz doubted the October 670 call and 660 put were bought as a combination because of the cost.
The October 660 put had a premium of 8-3/8, down 1/4 from Wednesday and the October 670 call had a premium of 6-1/4, up 1/8 from Wednesday.

"I don't think people are buying the out-of-the-money calls and out-of-the-money puts as a combination because it's too expensive," Schwartz said. "It could represent a lot of people taking out-of-the-money positions for big moves in either direction."
He added that the U.S. Federal Reserve's inaction on interest rates earlier this week could be one reason investors are playing both sides of the market.
On the S&P 500 stock index .SPX, calls were more in demand than the puts, with 54,631 calls trading compared with 45,275 puts.
The spot SPX index ended up a fraction at 685.86 after bounding between 683.77 and 690.15.
The most active option was the October 620 call, which traded roughly 8,425 contracts. The option, with open interest of 4,760, rose two to 70.
The SPX November 650 put traded about 6,260 contracts, the corresponding call traded 6,000. The November 600 put traded 6,010 contracts and its corresponding call traded 6,200.
Traders said most of that activity was a series of spreads, most notably two blocks of 6,000 on the November 650 call and the November 600 put.
